**Monday, August 24, 1931**

August 24 is a date with a long memory. In the year 79, it was the day Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii — a city frozen mid-morning, mid-meal, mid-sentence, preserved for eighteen centuries before excavators found it and gave it back to history. In 1814, it was the day British forces marched into Washington and burned the Capitol and the White House. The date keeps arriving with weight it didn't ask for. On August 24, 1931, it arrived again, and you were born into it.

---

**The world at your birth**

What the Great Depression felt like in the summer of 1931 is worth sitting with. By August, roughly eight million Americans were out of work, and the number was climbing toward what would eventually be one in four. The farm economy had collapsed years before the stock market — agricultural prices had been falling since the early 1920s — so rural America was already hollowed out before the crash. In cities, the breadlines and soup kitchens that would define the decade's imagery were already running. Men who had owned businesses in 1928 were selling apples from carts.

What made 1931 distinctive, even within the Depression, was that the banking system itself was beginning to disintegrate. More than 2,000 American banks had failed in 1931 alone by the time you were born, and the pace was accelerating. When a bank failed, the deposits vanished — there was no federal insurance. Families lost everything they had saved, not because they had speculated, but because they had trusted institutions that turned out to be hollow.

This was the economic air of the room you entered.

---

**Twenty-eight days after you were born**

On September 21, 1931 — when you were less than a month old — Britain abandoned the gold standard. For decades, the pound had been pegged to gold at a fixed rate, and the international financial system had been organized around that peg. The decision to float was treated at the time as an emergency measure, a sign of catastrophic strain. It was. But it also marked the beginning of the end of the financial architecture that had governed the world economy since the nineteenth century. The global monetary order under which your parents had lived their entire lives was dismantled in the first weeks of yours.

Four weeks after that, on October 18, the George Washington Bridge opened between New York and New Jersey — the longest suspension bridge in the world. In the same autumn: new banks failing, new breadlines forming, and the longest bridge anyone had built. The Depression did not stop construction. It happened alongside everything else.

---

**Twenty-five days after you were born**

On September 18, 1931, Japanese officers staged an explosion on the South Manchuria Railway and used it to justify an invasion of Manchuria. The Mukden Incident was fabricated — the explosion was their own — but it didn't matter. The League of Nations condemned Japan; Japan withdrew from the League. No consequence followed. That impunity was itself a lesson, absorbed by governments across the world. You were three weeks old when the chain of events that would lead to Pearl Harbor quietly opened.

---

**Your sixtieth birthday**

On August 24, 1991 — the day you turned sixty — Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

A coup had been attempted against him four days earlier by Communist hardliners determined to stop his reforms. It collapsed within three days. On August 24th, facing a party that had tried to remove him and a country that was dissolving around it, Gorbachev stepped down from the Party leadership and suspended its activities. The Soviet Union itself would formally dissolve on Christmas Day.

You were born in 1931, when the Communist Party of the Soviet Union was a rising force reshaping global politics, and when the Great Depression was making liberal democracy look fragile and capitalism look broken. Fascism and communism both presented themselves that year as answers to a question that capitalism seemed to be failing to answer. You turned sixty on the day the Communist answer effectively ended.

That is a span.

---

**What you have witnessed**

You are 95 years old. The list of what did not yet exist when you were born is so long it begins to sound like fiction: the New Deal, Social Security, penicillin as a widely available medicine, jet aircraft, nuclear weapons, the polio vaccine, television as a mass medium, the interstate highway system, commercial computers, space travel, the civil rights legislation of the 1960s, the internet, the smartphone, and now artificial intelligence composing text in response to a name and a date.

You were two years old when Hitler became chancellor of Germany. You were thirteen when the atomic bombs fell on Japan and the war ended. You were seventeen when Israel was established and the Berlin Airlift began. You were twenty-eight when the first satellite went into orbit. You were thirty-eight when humans walked on the Moon. You were fifty-eight when the Berlin Wall fell. You were seventy on September 11, 2001.

The Pompeii that Vesuvius buried on your birthday's date in the year 79 had been a prosperous Roman city at the height of empire, its residents going about ordinary business on an ordinary morning. The excavations that returned it to view began in earnest in the eighteenth century. The archaeologists found bread still in the ovens.

The world you entered on August 24, 1931 is gone in ways nearly as complete. The institutions, the technologies, the political map, the daily textures of life — nearly all of it replaced or transformed. You have watched most of the replacement happen.

Ninety-five years. The date keeps arriving. You keep receiving it.
